before:
उसी प्रकार बोधिसत्त्व के उत्तम गुणों को धारण करने वाले,
योग में यत्न करते हुए ध्यान और समाधि में स्थित होकर,
पुनः कामधातु में स्थित होते हैं और अनासक्त रहते हैं;
जल में पद्म की भाँति, वे मूर्खों के बाल-गुणों में स्थित नहीं होते।
after:
उसी प्रकार बोधिसत्त्व के उत्तम गुणों को धारण करने वाले,
योग में उद्योग करते हुए ध्यान और समाधि में स्थित होकर,
पुनः कामधातु में स्थित होकर भी अनासक्त रहते हैं;
जल में पद्म की भाँति, वे मूर्खों के बाल-गुणों में स्थित नहीं होते।

before:
उसी प्रकार, विद्वान् बोधिसत्त्व प्रीति और,
सुख प्रदान करने वाले चार शान्त ध्यानों तथा समाधियों को प्राप्त करके,
ध्यान-सुख से युक्त ध्यान तथा समाधि की प्राप्ति को त्यागकर,
जगत् के प्रति करुणा से युक्त हो पुनः कामधातु में प्रवेश करते हैं।
after:
उसी प्रकार, विद्वान् बोधिसत्त्व, जो प्रीति और
सुख प्रदान करते हैं, चार शान्त ध्यानों तथा समाधियों को प्राप्त करके,
ध्यान-सुख से युक्त ध्यान तथा समाधि की प्राप्ति को त्यागकर,
जगत् के प्राणियों के प्रति करुणा से युक्त हो पुनः कामधातु में प्रवेश करते हैं।

before:
अन्य सत्त्वों तथा पुद्गलों के लिए विशुद्ध बोधिसत्त्व,
वीर्यपारमिता में प्रत्यक्ष उद्योग करते हुए विचरण करता है;
उदाहरणार्थ, जैसे जल भरती दासी स्वतन्त्र नहीं, स्वामी के अधीन होती है,
उसी प्रकार वीर सर्वसत्त्वों के अधीन होकर चलते हैं।
after:
अन्य सत्त्वों तथा पुद्गलों के लिए विशुद्ध बोधिसत्त्व,
वीर्यपारमिता में तत्परता से लगे हुए विचरण करता है;
उदाहरणार्थ, जैसे जल भरती दासी स्वतन्त्र नहीं, स्वामी के अधीन होती है,
उसी प्रकार वीर सर्वसत्त्वों के अधीन होकर चलते हैं।

before:
अपने सुख को त्याग कर आशारहित चित्त से,
अन्य सत्त्वों के प्रयोजन हेतु दिन-रात प्रत्यक्ष उद्योग करें;
जैसे माता अपने इकलौते पुत्र की परिचर्या करती है,
सच्चे हृदय से बिना किसी खेद के स्थित रहें।
after:
अपने सुख को त्याग कर आशारहित चित्त से,
अन्य सत्त्वों के प्रयोजन हेतु दिन-रात तत्परता से लगे रहें;
जैसे माता अपने इकलौते पुत्र की परिचर्या करती है,
सच्चे हृदय से बिना किसी खेद के स्थित रहें।

before:
जो भी बोधिसत्त्व क्षान्ति के उत्तम धर्म से युक्त है,
जो त्रिसाहस्र लोकधातु को रत्नों से भरकर लोकविद्,
बुद्धों, अर्हतों और प्रत्येकबुद्धों को अर्पित करता है,
दान का वह स्कन्ध उसके पुण्य के अंश की भी बराबरी नहीं कर सकता।
after:
जो भी बोधिसत्त्व क्षान्ति के उत्तम धर्म से युक्त है,
जो त्रिसाहस्र लोकधातु को रत्नों से भरकर
लोकविद् बुद्धों, अर्हतों और प्रत्येकबुद्धों को अर्पित करता है,
दान का वह स्कन्ध उसके पुण्य के अंश की भी बराबरी नहीं कर सकता।

before:
जो भी विशुद्ध सत्त्व इस प्रकार शीलवान् है,
वह प्रिय और अप्रिय सभी के प्रति दृष्टिरहित होता है;
सिर और हाथ-पैर दान करते हुए भी उसका चित्त दीन नहीं होता,
और अपना सर्वस्व दान करते हुए वह सदा आसक्ति से मुक्त रहता है।
after:
जो भी विशुद्ध सत्त्व इस प्रकार शीलवान् है,
वह प्रिय और अप्रिय सभी के प्रति अपेक्षा-रहित होता है;
सिर और हाथ-पैर दान करते हुए भी उसका चित्त दीन नहीं होता,
और अपना सर्वस्व दान करते हुए वह सदा आसक्ति से मुक्त रहता है।

before:
तीन भव में अशेष जितने भी सत्त्व हैं,
पूरी तरह विचार कर कि वे सभी
लोकविद् बुद्धों, अर्हतों और प्रत्येकबुद्धों को
अनन्त कल्पों तक दान दें और भली-भांति श्रावक की खोज करें;
after:
तीन भव में अशेष जितने भी सत्त्व हैं,
उन्हें कल्पना की चरम सीमा मानकर, यदि वे सभी
लोकविद् बुद्धों, अर्हतों और प्रत्येकबुद्धों को
अनन्त कल्पों तक दान दें और भली-भाँति श्रावक की बोधि की खोज करें;

before:
यदि बोधिसत्त्व जगत् के प्राणियों को दान देकर,
उसमें ममकार नहीं करता और वस्तु के प्रति खेद नहीं करता,
तो उससे कुशलमूल महान शक्ति से बढ़ते हैं,
जैसे मेघरहित, प्रकाशमान शुक्ल पक्ष का चन्द्रमण्डल।
after:
यदि बोधिसत्त्व जगत् के प्राणियों को दान देकर,
उसमें ममकार नहीं करता और वस्तु के प्रति कृपणता या आसक्ति नहीं रखता,
तो उससे कुशलमूल महान शक्ति से बढ़ते हैं,
जैसे मेघरहित, प्रकाशमान शुक्ल पक्ष का चन्द्रमण्डल।

before: If a tree has no sprout, it will never grow in the world. Without a tree, how could branches, leaves, flowers, and fruit ever appear? It is the same without the wish to awaken. Without it, a Victorious One would never appear in the world. And without their awakening, how could the good fruits, like Shakra, Brahma, and the listeners, ever appear?
after: If there is no sprout, a tree could never grow in the world. Without a tree, how could branches, leaves, flowers, and fruit ever appear? In the same way, without the wish to awaken, a Victorious One would never appear in the world. Without a Victorious One, how could the fruits—like Shakra, Brahma, and listeners—ever appear?

before: This teaching of the Guides is deep and hard to see. No one can just figure it out or reach it. So, when the Kind Helper reached awakening, he paused. He thought, "Who among all the living beings will understand this?"
after: This teaching of the Guides is deep and hard to see. No one has realized it, and no one has reached it. So, when the Kind Helper reached awakening, he paused. He thought, "Who among all the living beings will understand this?"

before: There are many harmful spirits and sicknesses in the human world. A person with compassion can calm them through the blessing of truth. Even so, they feel no self-importance and do not show pride. You should know they have a prediction of never turning back.
after: There are many diseases and harmful spirits in the human world. People with compassion calm them through a blessing of truth. Even so, these helpers feel no self-importance and do not give rise to pride. You should know they have a prediction of never turning back.

before: But maybe someone performs a blessing of truth and feels self-importance. They might proudly think, 'I have a prediction!' Or they might feel self-importance when other awakening heroes give them a prediction. Anyone who holds onto this self-importance has little understanding.
after: But someone might perform a blessing of truth and feel self-importance, thinking, "I have a prediction." Or they might feel self-importance because other awakening heroes made a prediction about them. You should know that anyone who stays stuck in self-importance has little understanding.

before: Mara might approach you and use names to trick you. He will say, 'These are the names of you and your parents. These are the names of your ancestors for seven generations. When you become a Buddha, this will be your name.'
after: Sometimes Mara approaches someone and tries to trick them using names. He says, "These are the names of you and your parents. These are the names of your family going back seven generations. And when you become a Buddha, this will be your name."

before: Mara will tell you about your strict practices and your training. He will say, 'You had these same good qualities in the past.' An awakening hero might hear this and feel self-importance. If they do, they are being pushed by Mara and have little understanding.
after: Mara tells them about the strict practices and training they will do. He says, "Your past good qualities and actions were just like this, too." If any awakening hero hears these words and feels self-importance, Mara has completely tricked them. You should know they have little understanding.

before: Someone might live far away in quiet villages, cities, and mountain valleys. They might stay deep in the forest or in hidden retreats. Even so, an awakening hero might praise themselves and put down others. You should know that such a person is pushed by Mara and has little understanding.
after: An awakening hero might live far away in lonely villages, cities, or mountain valleys. They might stay in a deep forest or a quiet woodland retreat. But if they praise themselves and put down others, Mara has completely tricked them. You should know they have little understanding.

before: They might always live right in the middle of busy villages and towns. But they only work toward awakening and helping living beings grow. They do not wish to become a worthy one or a solitary Buddha. This is what is called the quiet aloneness of a son of the Well-Gone One.
after: A true hero might always live among people in villages, provinces, and towns. They only work hard for awakening and for helping living beings grow. They do not wish to become a worthy one or a solitary Buddha. This way of living is taught as the quiet aloneness of a son of the Well-Gone One.

before: An awakening hero might live for millions of years in a snake-filled mountain valley five hundred leagues wide. But if they do not understand true quiet aloneness, they will only end up feeling better than others and living mixed up in the world.
after: Someone might sit in a mountain cave five hundred leagues wide. They might sit with snakes for millions of years. But an awakening hero must understand true quiet aloneness. If they do not, they only end up feeling better than others. They stay mixed up in the world.

before: An awakening hero might work hard for the benefit of beings. They might gain deep focus, powers, abilities, freedoms, and deep calm. But someone might look down on them and think, "This person does not practice in the quiet forest." The Victorious One has said that anyone who thinks this is living in Mara's domain.
after: An awakening hero might work hard to help beings. They might gain deep focus, power, ability, freedom, and deep calm. Someone might look down on them and say, "This person does not practice in the quiet forest." The Victorious One says this proud person lives in Mara's domain.

before: A person might live in a village or in a forest. If they are free from the mind of the two vehicles and sure of the highest awakening, this is the quiet aloneness of those who work for the good of beings. An awakening hero who judges them only ruins themselves.
after: A person might live in a busy village or in a forest. They might leave behind the goals of the two vehicles and aim only for the highest awakening. This is true quiet aloneness for those working for the good of beings. An awakening hero ruins their own path if they judge others.

before: Therefore, a wise person seeking the highest awakening must have a strong purpose and completely destroy their pride. Think of how sick people rely on a doctor to get well. In the same way, this wise person should carefully rely on a wise friend.
after: Therefore, a wise person who seeks the highest awakening must be strong. They must completely destroy their pride. Think of sick people trying to get well. They must trust a doctor to cure them. In the same way, you must carefully trust a wise friend.

before: Buddhas and awakening heroes who have entered the highest awakening, along with the perfections, should be relied upon as wise friends. They are the teachers, and this is the level of accomplishment. By these two causes, a Buddha's awakening is quickly reached.
after: Buddhas and awakening heroes have entered the highest awakening. You should trust them and every perfection as a wise friend. They are the teachers, and this is the level of accomplishment. These are the two causes. Through them, a Buddha's awakening is quickly reached.

before: Think of the Victorious Ones of the past, the future, and those living in the ten directions. This perfection is the path for all of them, and there is no other. For those who have entered into the highest awakening, this perfection is explained as their brightness, lamp, light, and greatest teacher.
after: Think of every Victorious One in the past, the future, and the ten directions. This perfection is the only path for all of them. Are you stepping toward the highest awakening? Then this perfection is your brightness, your lamp, and your light. It is your greatest teacher.

before: The defining feature of perfect wisdom is that it is empty. All things have this same defining feature. If you clearly know things are empty and without signs, you practice well. This is the wisdom practice of the Well-Gone Ones.
after: The defining feature of perfect wisdom is being empty. You should know that the defining feature of all these things is just like that. You must see clearly that things are empty and without signs. Practicing in this way is the wisdom practice of the Well-Gone Ones.

before: Living beings have many thoughts and want food. Those attached to the cycle of rebirth wander forever. Both self and things of a self are not real and empty. Still, the unwise tie knots in the sky.
after: Living beings have many thoughts and desire food. Those whose minds cling to the cycle of rebirth wander forever. Both the self and the things of a self are not real and are empty. Yet the unwise act as if they are tying knots in the sky.

before: For example, someone might have the idea that they swallowed poison. Even if no poison went inside them, they still faint. In the same way, the unwise believe in self and what belongs to self. Because of this false idea, they are born and die in a world that is always changing.
after: For example, someone might have the idea that they drank poison. They will faint even if no poison actually entered their body. The unwise act just like this. They insist on a self and what belongs to self. Because of this untrue idea of a self, they keep being born and dying in an always changing world.

before: Where there is clinging, I teach there is complete mental trouble. When you do not find self and what belongs to self, this is becoming completely clean. In truth, nothing gets mental trouble or becomes pure. Knowing this, the awakening hero realizes perfect wisdom.
after: Wherever there is clinging, complete mental trouble is taught. When you do not find a self and what belongs to self, this is called becoming completely clean. Truly, there is no thing that gets mental trouble or becomes pure. When an awakening hero understands this, they realize perfect wisdom.

before: Imagine every single one of the living beings in Jambudvipa. Suppose they all form the wish for highest awakening. Suppose they practice generosity for millions of years. Then they dedicate all this as a cause of awakening to help beings.
after: Think of all the living beings in Jambudvipa without exception. Imagine if all of them were to form the wish for highest awakening. They might practice generosity for millions of years. They could dedicate all of this as a cause of awakening to help all beings.

before: Now think of someone who tries hard to practice the highest perfect wisdom. They follow it for just one day. All that generosity from before cannot match a tiny part of this person's stored-up goodness. Therefore, you should always practice wisdom and never be lazy.
after: Now imagine someone who works hard at the highest perfect wisdom. They might follow it for just a single day. All of that generosity cannot match even a tiny piece of this person's stored-up goodness. Because of this, you should always practice wisdom without being lazy.

before: A meditator who practices the highest perfect wisdom feels great compassion. Yet, they do not hold the idea of living beings. At that time, this wise person becomes a worthy recipient for all beings. They always consume their alms in a meaningful way.
after: A meditator practices the highest perfect wisdom. They feel great compassion, but they do not hold onto the idea of living beings. Because of this, the wise meditator becomes a worthy recipient for all beings. Whenever they eat the alms given by the world, it is truly meaningful.

before: An awakening hero wants to set free the living beings in the god and human worlds and the three lower realms. To show these living beings the wide path to the other shore, they must strive day and night in perfect wisdom.
after: An awakening hero might want to set free the living beings in the god and human worlds and the three lower realms. They want to show all living beings the wide path to the other shore. To do this, they must try hard day and night in perfect wisdom.

before: Imagine a person who finally finds the highest jewel. Out of joy, they become careless and lose it right away. Because it is lost, they miss the jewel. They endure constant suffering.
after: Imagine someone finds the highest jewel after never having one before. They might get so happy that they become careless right away and lose it. Because it is lost, they feel constant suffering as they wish for their jewel back.

before: In the same way, someone seeking the highest awakening must not give up their training in perfect wisdom. Perfect wisdom is like a jewel. Think of a person who finds a jewel, wraps it carefully, and walks swiftly on their way to reach peace.
after: In the same way, someone who has entered the highest awakening must not give up their training in perfect wisdom. Perfect wisdom is like a jewel. Think of a person who finds a jewel, wraps it up carefully, and travels quickly on their way until they reach peace.

before: The sun comes out from behind the clouds with a net of bright rays. As it rises, it destroys all the deep, pitch-black darkness. The sun outshines all the fireflies and all living creatures. It also outshines the stars and the light of the moon.
after: Think of the bright sun rising in a sky without clouds. Its rays completely destroy the thick, dark night. As it shines, it outshines all the little fireflies and living creatures. It even outshines all the stars and the bright light of the moon.

before: In the same way, an awakening hero practices the highest perfect wisdom. They practice emptiness and act without signs. This wise person destroys the thick darkness of views. They outshine all beings, worthy ones, solitary Buddhas, and many other awakening heroes.
after: In the same way, an awakening hero practices the highest perfect wisdom. They practice emptiness and act without signs. By doing this, the wise hero destroys the thick darkness of wrong view. They outshine all beings, worthy ones, solitary Buddhas, and many other awakening heroes.

before: Think of a prince who wants to give away his riches. He becomes a great leader, and people want to be near him. Even as a prince, he brings joy to many living beings. Imagine how much more he will do when he learns clever ways and becomes the king!
after: Think of a prince who wants to give away his wealth. He becomes a great leader that everyone wants to meet. Even now, he brings joy to many living beings. Imagine how much more he will do when he learns clever ways and rules the kingdom!

before: In the same way, an awakening hero who is skilled in practicing wisdom gives the nectar of deathlessness. This brings joy to gods and humans. Even now, they work hard to help many living beings. Just imagine how much more they will do when they become a King of the Teaching!
after: In the same way, an awakening hero who is skilled in practicing wisdom gives the nectar of deathlessness. They bring joy to gods and humans. Even now, they work hard to help many living beings. Imagine how much more they will do when they become a King of the Teaching!

before: When this happens, Mara feels like he has been poked by a sharp thorn. He is filled with sadness, suffering, worry, and weakness. He wonders how he can make this awakening hero give up. Trying to scare them, he sets fires all around and throws flaming stars from the sky.
after: At that time, Mara hurts as if poked by a thorn. He is full of sadness, suffering, worry, and weakness. He thinks, "How can I make this awakening hero give up?" He sets the sky on fire and throws shooting stars to scare them.

before: These wise ones have very strong minds. Day and night, they look at the highest meaning of perfect wisdom. Then, their body, mind, and speech move as freely as a bird in the sky. How could any helper of the Dark One ever find a chance to stop them?
after: When these wise ones are truly determined, they see the high meaning of perfect wisdom day and night. Then their body, mind, and speech move as freely as a bird in the sky. How could any helper of the Dark One find a chance to stop them?

before: But sometimes awakening heroes fight and argue. They get mad at each other and do not get along. When this happens, Mara rejoices and becomes very happy. He thinks, 'Those two will drift far away from the deep knowing of the Victorious Ones.'
after: When awakening heroes fight and argue, they stay mad and do not get along. At that time, Mara rejoices and becomes very happy. He thinks, "Those two will wander far away from the deep knowing of the Victorious Ones."

before: Those two will drift far away and act like flesh-eating monsters. They will both break their own promises. How could anyone reach awakening if they are angry and have no patience? At that time, the Maras and all their friends will celebrate.
after: Those two will wander far away and act like flesh-eating monsters. They will both break their own promises. How can there be awakening for those who are mean and lack patience? At that time, the Maras and their followers will rejoice.

before: Suppose an awakening hero who has not yet received a prediction gets angry. If they start a fight with one who has received a prediction, they lose time. For every single moment they hold onto this bad thought, they must put on their armor and start over for that many ages.
after: Imagine an awakening hero who has not received a prediction. If they get angry and fight with someone who has a prediction, they have bad thoughts. For every single angry moment, they must put on their armor from the very beginning. They will have to start over for that many ages.

before: A Buddha reaches awakening through the perfection of patience. Good learners use careful attention and think, "This mind is not good." They own up to their mistakes and stop themselves from repeating them. They do not enjoy bad thoughts. In this way, they train in a Buddha's qualities.
after: A Buddha reaches awakening through the perfection of patience. Learners use careful attention and think, "This mind is not good." They own up to their mistakes. They promise to stop themselves next time. They do not enjoy bad thoughts. This is how they train in a Buddha's qualities.

before: When doing their training, some might cling to the training itself, but that is not so here. They do not grasp at a learner or at the things to train in. They do not think of training and not training as two different things. Anyone who practices like this is training in a Buddha's qualities.
after: When they practice, they do not hold onto any training at all. They do not hold onto a learner or the things to train in. They do not think about training and not training. A person who practices like this trains in a Buddha's qualities.

before: Any awakening hero who knows this training will never ruin it or lose their good conduct. They practice this to gain a Buddha's qualities. They are skilled in the higher training, and they know there is nothing to hold onto.
after: An awakening hero who understands this training will never ruin it. They will never lose their good conduct. They practice this to gain a Buddha's qualities. They are highly skilled at the higher training. They know there is nothing to hold onto.

before: By training in the wisdom of the wise light-makers, they do not have a single thought that is not good. Think of the sun moving across the sky. When the sun's bright rays shine, darkness cannot stay in the space before it.
after: They practice the wisdom of the wise light-makers in this way. They do not create even a single thought that is not good. Think of the sun moving high up in the sky. Its bright rays completely wipe out the shadows. Darkness cannot stay in the empty space before it.

before: When someone trains in perfect wisdom, every other perfection is included right there. All sixty-two views are included inside the mistaken view of a self. In the same way, the Buddha teaches that all the other perfections are included inside this one.
after: For those who have trained in perfect wisdom, every other perfection is included right here. The mistaken view of a self contains all the sixty-two views. In the exact same way, it is taught that every perfection is included right inside this wisdom.

before: When the life force stops, every other ability stops too. In the same way, for the great wise ones who practice wisdom, all the perfections are gathered right here.
after: For example, when the life force stops, all other abilities stop too, no matter how many there are. In the same way, for the great wise ones who practice wisdom, all the perfections are gathered into this one.

before: Wise awakening heroes train in every good quality of a listener. They also train in all the good qualities of a solitary Buddha. They do not get stuck in them or wish for them. They just think, "This is what I must learn," and so they train.
after: Wise awakening heroes train in all the good qualities that listeners have. They also train in all the good qualities of the solitary Buddhas. But they do not stay stuck in these qualities or want them for themselves. They just think, "This is what I must train in," and so they train.

before: Some beings have fully entered into awakening with no turning back. If you truly rejoice in their making the wish to awaken, your goodness is huge. You could weigh Mount Meru of this vast system of worlds on a scale. But you cannot weigh the goodness of that rejoicing.
after: Some people fully enter into the highest awakening with no turning back. If you rejoice deep in your heart when they are making the wish to awaken, you create great goodness. You could measure the huge Mount Meru of this vast system of worlds by weighing it on a scale, but you cannot weigh the goodness when you rejoice like that.

before: Many living beings look for goodness and want to help others. One should also rejoice in the heap of stored-up goodness of them all. Because of this, once they gain every good quality of the Victorious Ones, they give the gift of teaching to the world to end suffering.
after: There are many living beings who look for goodness and want to help others. You should also rejoice in the heap of stored-up goodness of them all. Because of this, when they gain the good qualities of the Victorious Ones, they will give the gift of teaching to the world to end suffering.

before: An awakening hero without made-up thoughts fully knows all things. They know things are empty, without signs, and free from tangled thinking. They do not seek awakening with a wisdom that splits things in two. That meditator works hard in the highest perfect wisdom.
after: An awakening hero is without made-up thoughts and fully knows that all things are empty, without signs, and free from tangled thinking. This awakening hero does not look for awakening using a wisdom that splits things in two. Instead, that meditator works hard at the highest perfect wisdom.

before: The element of space and anything that goes against space do not exist. No one has ever attained it. In the same way, the awakening hero skilled in the practice of wisdom is like space. They practice complete peace.
after: The element of space and anything that goes against that space do not exist, and no one has ever caught it. In the same way, the awakening hero who is skilled in the practice of wisdom is just like space, and practices complete peace.

before: Think of a person made by magic standing in a crowd. This illusion does not think, "I must make these people happy." But they do it anyway! People see them showing off many magic powers. Yet they have no body, no mind, and not even a name.
after: Think of an illusion, like a person made by magic standing in a crowd. They do not think, "I must please these people," but they still do it. You can see them showing off different magic powers. Even so, they have no body, no mind, and not even a name.

before: In the same way, those who practice wisdom never think, "After I reach awakening, I will completely free all beings." They take on many kinds of births and do many things. They show these things like an illusion. Yet they practice without fixed ideas.
after: It is the same for those who practice wisdom. They never think, "After I reach awakening, I will free all beings." They take on different kinds of birth and do many things. They show these actions like an illusion, but they practice without fixed ideas.

before: For example, a magic copy of a Buddha performs a Buddha's deed. But it feels no pride at all. In the same way, an awakening hero is skilled in practicing wisdom. They show all their actions like a magic creation and an illusion.
after: Think of a magic copy of a Buddha. It does a Buddha's deed without feeling any pride at all. In the same way, an awakening hero who is skilled in practicing wisdom acts just like a magic creation and an illusion.

before: A skilled carpenter makes figures that look like men and women. These figures can do all kinds of tasks. In the same way, an awakening hero is skilled in practicing wisdom. They do all their actions through deep knowing free of thoughts.
after: A clever woodworker can make wooden figures of men and women. These figures can do all kinds of work. In the same way, an awakening hero who is skilled in practicing wisdom does everything through deep knowing free of thoughts.

before: When someone is skilled in practicing like this, a huge crowd of gods will put palms together. They bow down and show respect. There are many Buddhas in the world systems of the ten directions. All these Buddhas speak endless praise for their good qualities.
after: When someone practices so well, a great crowd of gods will put palms together. They bow down and show respect. All the Buddhas in the world systems of the ten directions sing praises for their good qualities.

before: Think of all the living beings in worlds as many as the Ganges. Suppose they all decided to become Maras. Suppose each one made even more Maras from every single hair! Even then, they could not make obstacles for the wise.
after: Think of all the living beings in worlds as countless as the sands of the Ganges. If they all became Maras, and made even more Maras from every hair on their bodies, they still could not create obstacles for the wise.

before: A wise awakening hero is strong because of four causes. The four Maras cannot beat them or shake them. First, they rest in emptiness. Second, they never give up on living beings. Third, they do exactly what they say. Fourth, they have the blessing of the Well-Gone Ones.
after: A wise awakening hero is strong because of four causes. Because of these, the four Maras cannot defeat or shake them. First, they rest in emptiness. Second, they do not leave living beings behind. Third, they do exactly as they say. Fourth, they have the blessing of the Well-Gone Ones.

before: This perfect wisdom is the Mother of the Thus-Gone Ones. When it is taught, an awakening hero might wish to learn it. If they try hard to master it with a true heart, you should know something about this noble person. They have stepped onto the path of knowing everything.
after: Perfect wisdom is the Mother of the Thus-Gone Ones. When it is taught, an awakening hero might wish to learn it. They might work hard to practice it with a true heart. You should know this noble person has stepped into knowing everything.

before: They do not stay stuck in the expanse of all things or the way things really are. Instead, they rest without resting, just like a cloud in the sky. Think of a holder of magic words flying through the air. If they want to rest, they use words of power to grow flowers out of season. Then they bless the spot just as they please.
after: They do not rest in the expanse of all things or the way things really are. Instead, they rest without resting, like a cloud in the sky. Think of a holder of magic words traveling in the sky without a home. If they wish to stay somewhere, they use their words of power. They can make flowers bloom out of season and bless the place just as they wish.

before: When practicing like this, a wise and bright awakening hero does not cling to the mind that understands. They do not cling to a Buddha's qualities. They do not grasp at a teacher, a person who wants the teaching, or someone with a certain view. This is how people live when they want peace and love every good quality.
after: Practicing like this, the wise and bright awakening hero does not grasp at the mind that understands. They do not grasp at a Buddha's qualities. They do not grasp at a teacher, a person who wants the teaching, or someone holding a view. This is how people rest when they want peace and delight in every good quality.

before: A listener or a solitary Buddha can rest in deep calm. Their rest is very peaceful and full of joy. But the way an awakening hero rests is even better than all of those. It is the very best, beaten only by the freedom of a worthy one or a Thus-Gone One.
after: Listeners and solitary Buddhas rest in deep calm. Their rest is deeply peaceful and full of joy, no matter how many there are. But this way of resting is the highest and best of them all. It is second only to the freedom of the worthy ones and the Thus-Gone Ones.

before: Birds live in the sky, but they do not fall. Fish live in the water, but they do not drown. In the same way, an awakening hero uses the power of deep focus to reach the far shore. They rest in emptiness, but they do not slip away into peace beyond sorrow.
after: Birds live in the sky, but they do not fall. Fish live in the water, but they do not drown and die. In the same way, the awakening hero uses the power of deep focus. They reach the far shore and rest in emptiness. Still, they do not pass into peace beyond sorrow.

before: Some may wish to reach the highest good qualities of all living beings. They may want to touch a Buddha's deep knowing, which is supreme and wonderful. They may wish to give the best and holiest gift of teaching. To do this, they should rely on this perfect home of the helpers.
after: Someone might want to reach the highest good qualities of all living beings. They might want to touch a Buddha's deep knowing, which is amazing and supreme. They might wish to give the best and holy gift of teaching. That person should rely on this supreme home of the helpers.

before: The Guides teach about many trainings. But this training is the highest and best of them all. A wise person may wish to go to the far shore of all trainings. To do this, they should train in perfect wisdom. This is the training of the Buddhas.
after: When the Guides explain all the trainings, this training is the very best. It is higher than any other training. A wise person might want to reach the far shore of all trainings. They should practice this training in perfect wisdom. This is the training of the Buddhas.

before: This is the supreme treasure of teaching and the holy treasury of the teaching. It is the Buddha family. It is a treasury of happiness and joy for beings. The Protectors of the world live in the past, the future, and the ten directions. All of them are born from this. Yet the expanse of all things never runs out.
after: This is the supreme treasure of teaching and the holy treasury of the teaching. It is the Buddha family. It is a treasury of happiness and joy for beings. The Protectors of the world live in the past, the future, and the ten directions. All of them come from this. Even so, the expanse of all things never runs out.

before: Think of all the trees, fruits, flowers, and forests. They all perfectly arise and come from the earth. Yet the earth itself is never used up, and it does not grow larger. It never shrinks. It is without fixed ideas, and it never grows tired.
after: Think of all the trees, fruits, flowers, and forests. They all grow and come up from the earth. But the earth is never used up, and it never gets bigger. It does not shrink. It is without fixed ideas, and it never gets tired.

before: Think of the children of the Buddha, the listeners, the solitary Buddhas, and the gods. Think of all the happy and joyful things for beings. All of them arise from supreme perfect wisdom. Yet this wisdom is never used up, and it never grows larger.
after: Think of the children of the Buddha, the listeners, the solitary Buddhas, and the gods. Think of all the happy and joyful things for beings. They all come from supreme perfect wisdom. Yet this wisdom never runs out, and it never grows larger.

before: There are low, medium, and supreme living beings. The Well-Gone One taught that they all arise from ignorance. When helping causes come together, the machine of suffering fully arises. Yet that machine of ignorance is never used up, and it never grows larger.
after: There are many living beings, whether they are low, average, or great. The Well-Gone One taught that they all come from ignorance. When helping causes come together, the machine of suffering starts up. Yet that machine of ignorance never runs out and never grows larger.

before: There are many kinds of deep knowing, approaches, gateways, clever ways, and roots. They all come from supreme perfect wisdom. When helping causes gather, the machine of deeds starts to work. Yet perfect wisdom never runs out, and it never grows larger.
after: There are many kinds of deep knowing, gateways, clever ways, and roots. All of these come from supreme perfect wisdom. When helping causes come together, the machine of deeds appears. Yet perfect wisdom never runs out and never grows.

before: An awakening hero looks at things arising from causes together. Using this wisdom, they know things are never born and never end. A bright sun without clouds chases away the dark. Just like that sun, the hero destroys thick ignorance and reaches the state that has arisen by itself.
after: An awakening hero uses this wisdom to understand arising from causes together. They know it is never born and never runs out. A sun with no clouds shines light to chase away the dark. In the same way, the hero destroys thick ignorance and reaches the state that is arisen by itself.

before: These strong heroes rest in the four kinds of deep focus. But they do not lean on this deep focus or get stuck there. Even so, these four kinds of deep focus and every part of them help. They are the support for reaching supreme awakening.
after: These heroes have great power. They rest in the four kinds of deep focus. Yet they do not rely on them, and they do not truly stay in them. Still, these four kinds of deep focus and their parts act as a support. They help the hero reach supreme, wonderful awakening.

before: After reaching supreme wisdom, the awakening hero rests in deep focus. They also feel the four states of formless deep calm. This deep focus helps them reach supreme awakening. Yet the awakening hero does not train just to end their inner flaws.
after: They have supreme wisdom and rest in deep focus. They also feel the four wonderful kinds of formless deep calm. This deep focus helps them reach supreme, wonderful awakening. Yet the awakening hero does not train just to end their inner flaws.

before: Here is a great wonder about those who gather every good quality. They rest in deep focus and deep calm, but they see these states are without signs. When their bodies finally die, they are born again in the desire realm exactly where they want to be.
after: This is a great wonder of those who gather good qualities. They rest in deep focus and deep calm. They see that these states are without signs. If their bodies die while they rest there, they are born again in the desire realm. They are born exactly where they wish to be.

before: Imagine a person from Jambudvipa. They have never visited the great city of the gods. Later, this person travels there. They see the wonderful places owned by the gods. But when they return home, they do not feel attached to them.
after: Think of a person from Jambudvipa. They have never visited the supreme city of the gods in the realm of the gods. But later, they travel there. They see those places held by the gods. When they return here, they do not cling to them.

before: Awakening heroes hold the highest good qualities. They work hard at their training. They rest in deep focus and deep calm. Then they stay in the desire realm again without clinging to it. Like a lotus growing in water, they do not follow the ways of the unwise.
after: Like this, awakening heroes hold the highest good qualities. They work hard in their training. They rest in deep calm and deep focus. Then they live in the desire realm again without being attached. Like a lotus growing in water, they do not live by the ways of the unwise.

before: The great heroes act only to bring living beings to maturity. They make the lands pure and finish the perfections. They think, "My good qualities of awakening and my perfections would fade away." So, they do not try to be born in the formless realm.
after: Great heroes act only to bring living beings to maturity. They make the lands pure and finish the perfections. They think, 'The good qualities of awakening and the perfections would fade.' Because of this, they do not try to be born in the formless realm.

before: Think of a person who finds a treasure of jewels. They do not feel any greed for it. Later, they take the treasure with them. Even after taking it home, they do not cling to it.
after: Imagine a person who finds a hidden treasure of jewels. At first, they do not feel any desire for the jewels. Later on, they decide to take the whole treasure. They take the jewels and go home, but they do not become attached to them.

before: In the same way, wise awakening heroes give joy and happiness to others. They reach the four peaceful states of deep focus and deep calm. But they let go of the happiness of that deep focus. Full of compassion, they enter the desire realm again.
after: In the same way, wise awakening heroes give joy and happiness. They reach four peaceful states of deep calm and deep focus. Then they let go of the happiness from that deep calm and deep focus. Filled with compassion for others, they enter the desire realm again.

before: Suppose an awakening hero rests in deep calm and deep focus. But then they wish for the vehicle of a worthy one or a solitary Buddha. Then they are not settled in meditation. They become restless and have a wandering mind. A Buddha's good qualities completely fade away from them. They are like a boatman whose boat has crashed.
after: Suppose an awakening hero rests in deep calm and deep focus. But they start to want the vehicle of a worthy one or a solitary Buddha. Then they are not settled in meditation. They become restless and have a wandering mind. A Buddha's good qualities fade away from them, just like a sailor whose boat is wrecked.

before: They might experience form, sound, smell, taste, and touch. They might fully enjoy these five pleasures of the senses. But they stay away from the vehicle of the worthy one and the solitary Buddha. Instead, they find joy in the wish to awaken. You should know this hero is always resting in steady stillness.
after: Think about form, sound, smell, taste, and touch. These are the five pleasures of the senses. A hero might fully enjoy them. Yet they stay away from the vehicle of a worthy one or a solitary Buddha. Instead, they find joy in the wish to awaken. You should know this hero is always in steady stillness.

before: A pure awakening hero works hard in the perfection of steady effort for the sake of other living beings and persons. Think of a servant woman drawing water. She has no power of her own and must follow her master's orders. In the same way, these heroes act under the power of all living beings.
after: The pure awakening hero acts with the perfection of steady effort to help other living beings and persons. Think of a servant woman who draws water. She is completely under her master's power. In the same way, the heroes work under the power of all living beings.

before: Even if her master scolds or beats her all the time, the servant woman never talks back. She thinks, "He might even kill me!" Her mind is terrified, and she is overcome with fear.
after: Even if her master scolds or beats her, the servant woman does not say a word back. She thinks, 'He might even kill me.' She is deeply terrified and completely overcome with fear.

before: In the same way, those who walk the path to highest awakening for the sake of awakening should live like servants to all beings. This is how they reach awakening and perfect their good qualities. When a fire sparks from grass and wood, it burns up that very grass and wood.
after: In the same way, those who seek highest awakening for the sake of awakening should act like servants to all beings. This is how awakening is reached and good qualities are perfected. It is like a fire that starts from grass and wood. That same fire then burns up the grass and wood.

before: Let go of your own happiness and expect nothing in return. Work hard day and night for the needs of other living beings. Just as a mother takes care of her only child, you should help from the bottom of your heart without ever getting tired.
after: Let go of your own happiness and do not expect anything in return. Work hard day and night for what other living beings need. Care for them from the bottom of your heart, without ever getting tired. Do this just like a mother caring for her only child.

before: An awakening hero might wish to stay in the cycle of rebirth for a long time. Such a meditator works hard to help living beings and to finish the cleansing of the land. If not even a tiny speck of tiredness enters their mind, they have the perfection of steady effort and are never careless.
after: An awakening hero might wish to stay in the cycle of rebirth for a long time. Such a meditator works hard to help living beings and for the cleansing of the land. If they do not feel even a tiny speck of weariness, they have the perfection of steady effort and are never careless.

before: An unwise awakening hero counts tens of millions of ages. If they think reaching awakening will take a long time and bring suffering, they will feel suffering for a long time while practicing the true teaching. Because of this, their perfection of steady effort shrinks, and they are lazy.
after: An unwise awakening hero counts tens of millions of ages. They think the path to awakening is long and full of suffering. While trying to practice the true teaching, they will feel suffering for a long time. Because of this, their perfection of steady effort shrinks, and they become lazy.

before: Think about the time from when they first form the wish for highest awakening until they reach the awakening that nothing surpasses. If they feel like that whole long time is just a single day and night, you should know that these clear-minded, wise people have begun their steady effort.
after: They form the wish for highest awakening. Then they wait to reach the awakening that nothing surpasses. If they feel all this time is just a single day and night, they are clear-minded and wise. You should know they have begun their steady effort.

before: Someone might tell them, "You will reach highest awakening only after you smash Mount Meru to pieces." If they feel tired just thinking about how big that mountain is, then that awakening hero has become lazy.
after: Someone might say to them, 'You will reach highest awakening after you break down Mount Meru.' They might feel tired in their mind and worry about the mountain's size. If so, that awakening hero has become lazy.

before: But suppose they think, "What is so hard about that?" and decide to crush Mount Meru to dust in a single moment. That wise awakening hero has started their steady effort. Before long, they will reach the highest awakening of a Guide.
after: But they might think, 'What is so hard about an amount like this?' They might decide to crush Mount Meru to dust in just one moment. That wise awakening hero has begun their steady effort. Before long, they will reach the highest awakening of a Guide.

before: They might think, "I will help beings grow ready, and then I will work for their good." If they work hard at this with their body, speech, and mind, but still hold onto the idea of a self, they have actually become lazy. They are as far away from knowing everything as the sky is from the earth.
after: They might think, 'I will fully ripen beings and act to help them.' They might work hard at this with their body, speech, and mind. But if they hold on to the idea of a self, they have actually become lazy. They become as far away from knowing everything as the sky is from the earth.

before: Whenever they have no idea of a body, a mind, or living beings, they turn away from all ideas and practice the teaching that is not two. The Benefactor taught that this is the perfection of steady effort for those who want the highest, peaceful awakening that never fades away.
after: They might have no idea of a body, a mind, or living beings. They turn away completely from any idea, and they practice the teaching that is not two. The Benefactor has taught that this is the perfection of steady effort. It belongs to those who want the highest, peaceful, and endless awakening.

before: If they hear others saying bad things and using harsh words, the wise awakening hero thinks, "I am happy," and feels joy. They ask, "Who is speaking? Who is hearing? How is this said, what is being said, and why?" Having the highest perfection of patience, they are truly wise.
after: Others might speak badly and use harsh words. If a wise awakening hero hears this, they are glad and think, 'I am happy.' Who speaks? Who hears? By what is something said, what is said, and why? Since they have the highest perfection of patience, they are truly wise.

before: Imagine someone fills a vast system of worlds with jewels. They offer these to the Buddhas, the Knowers of the World. They also give them to worthy ones and solitary Buddhas. This mass of generosity is great. But it cannot match even a tiny part of the stored-up goodness of an awakening hero who has true patience.
after: An awakening hero has the excellent teaching of patience. Someone else might fill a vast system of worlds with jewels. They might offer these jewels to the Buddhas, the Knowers of the World, and to worthy ones and solitary Buddhas. But all that generosity cannot match even a tiny part of the patient hero's stored-up goodness.

before: The body of someone who rests in patience becomes completely pure. They gain the thirty-two marks and endless great strength. They speak the highest teaching of emptiness to living beings. Beings everywhere will feel joy to see this wise person who has patience.
after: The body of someone who rests in patience becomes completely pure. They have the thirty-two marks, endless power, and great strength. They share the highest teaching of emptiness with living beings. Wandering beings will rejoice in this wise person who has patience.

before: Suppose some living beings take sweet-smelling sandalwood. They rub it onto an awakening hero with great respect. At the same time, someone else drops burning coals on the hero's head. The awakening hero should keep an equal, calm mind toward both of them.
after: Some living beings might take a packet of sandalwood. They might rub it on the awakening hero with great respect. Someone else might throw burning coals on the hero's head. The awakening hero should keep an equal and even mind toward both of them.

before: The wise awakening hero practices patience in this way. After making the wish to awaken, they dedicate it to the highest awakening. By showing patience to the entire world, this hero shines brighter than the worthy ones. They outshine the solitary Buddhas and everyone in the realm of living beings.
after: The wise awakening hero practices patience in this way. They might dedicate their making the wish to awaken toward the highest awakening. By showing patience to the whole world, this hero outshines the worthy ones and solitary Buddhas. They outshine however many there are in the realm of living beings.

before: The person who practices patience should also think like this: 'There is much suffering in hell, as an animal, and in the world of Yama. I have helplessly suffered harm while chasing a pleasure of the senses. Why should I not practice patience now for the sake of awakening?'
after: The person who practices patience should also think like this. "There is much suffering in hell, among animals, and in the world of Yama. I have helplessly felt harm caused by the pleasures of the senses. Why should I not practice patience now for the sake of awakening?"

before: 'People might use whips, sticks, and weapons. They might beat me, tie me up, or try to kill me. They might even cut off my head, ears, hands, feet, and nose. But I will face all the suffering in the world with patience!' Thinking this, the awakening hero rests in the perfection of patience.
after: "People might use whips, sticks, and weapons. They might beat me, tie me up, or even kill me. They might cut off my head, ears, hands, feet, and nose. I will bear with patience whatever sufferings there are in the world!" Thinking this, the awakening hero rests in the perfection of patience.

before: Through good conduct, those who want peace become noble. They stay in the realm of the ten powers, and their good conduct is perfect. They follow all the actions of self-control. To help all living beings, they dedicate these actions to awakening.
after: Through good conduct, those who want peace become noble. They stay in the space of the ten powers. Their good conduct is never broken. They follow every kind of self-control. They dedicate all of this to awakening to help all living beings.

before: Someone might want to reach the awakening of a worthy one or a solitary Buddha. This person is unwise and is lacking good conduct, and their behavior falls apart. But someone else might dedicate their actions to the highest peace of awakening. Then, even while enjoying the pleasure of the senses, they stay in the perfection of good conduct.
after: If someone wants to reach the awakening of a worthy one or a solitary Buddha, they are lacking good conduct. They are foolish, and their actions fail. But they can dedicate their actions to the great peace of awakening instead. Then, even while enjoying a pleasure of the senses, they stay in the perfection of good conduct.

before: Some things always make the good qualities of awakening appear. For people with good qualities, this is the goal of good conduct. Other things ruin the awakening of those who try to help others. The Guide says this is lacking good conduct.
after: Some things surely make the good qualities of awakening grow. For those who have good qualities, this is the true goal of good conduct. Other things ruin the awakening of those who help others. The Guide has said that this is lacking good conduct.

before: An awakening hero might enjoy the five pleasures of the senses. But they have gone for refuge to the Buddha, the teaching, and the noble community. They turn their minds toward knowing everything. They think, "I must become a Buddha." You should understand that this wise person stays in the perfection of good conduct.
after: An awakening hero might enjoy the five pleasures of the senses. But they have taken refuge in the Buddha, the teaching, and the noble community. They focus their mind on knowing everything and think, "I must become a Buddha." You should know that this wise person stays in the perfection of good conduct.

before: Someone might practice the ten paths of good action for ten million ages. But they might desire to become a worthy one or a solitary Buddha. When they do, a flaw appears in their good conduct, and their good conduct breaks down. Making the wish to awaken in that way is much worse than a defeat.
after: Someone might practice the ten paths of good action for ten million ages. But they might start to want the state of a worthy one or a solitary Buddha. Right then, their good conduct is broken and falls apart. Making the wish to awaken in that way is worse than a defeat.

before: An awakening hero guards their good conduct and will dedicate it to the highest awakening. They feel no self-importance about this and do not praise themselves. They completely let go of the idea of a self and the idea of living beings. It is said that this awakening hero stays in the perfection of good conduct.
after: They protect their good conduct and dedicate it to the highest awakening. They have no self-importance about it and do not praise themselves. They completely let go of the idea of a self and the idea of living beings. Such an awakening hero is said to stay in the perfection of good conduct.

before: If an awakening hero walking the path of the Victorious Ones thinks, "These living beings are ones with good conduct, and those are lacking good conduct," they are completely lacking good conduct themselves because of this idea. Their own good conduct falls apart. They do not have perfectly pure good conduct.
after: An awakening hero might practice the path of the Victorious Ones and think, "These living beings are ones with good conduct, and these are lacking good conduct." By having these different ideas, they are entirely lacking good conduct. Their own good conduct breaks down, and they do not have pure good conduct.

before: Some have no idea of a self and no idea of living beings. Since they are free from any idea and free from wanting, how could they be not holding back? They have no self-importance about their self-control or their lack of self-control. The Guide taught that this is the good conduct of self-control.
after: Someone may have no idea of a self and no idea of living beings. If they are free from any idea and from wanting, how could they be not holding back? They have no self-importance about their self-control or their lack of self-control. The Guide taught that this is the good conduct of self-control.

before: Any pure living being who is one with good conduct does not focus on anything pleasant or unpleasant. Giving away their head, hands, and feet, they do not have a discouraged mind. Giving away everything they own, they are always free from holding on.
after: Any pure living being who is one with good conduct does not focus on pleasant or unpleasant things. If they give away their head, hands, and feet, they do not have a discouraged mind. When they give away everything they own, they are always free from holding on.

before: They know that things have a nature of no self and are not solid. If they give away even their own flesh without a discouraged mind, why even mention giving away outer objects? It is impossible for them to act with stinginess.
after: They know the nature of things is no self and not solid. If they give away even their own flesh without a discouraged mind, why even mention giving away outside objects? It is impossible for them to act with stinginess.

before: With an idea of a self, fools get attached by thinking of things as mine. How could they ever want to give? A stingy one will be born in the realm of hungry ghosts. Even if they are born as a human, they will be very poor.
after: People with the idea of a self become attached by thinking of things as mine. How could fools ever want to give? Stingy ones will be born in the realm of hungry ghosts. Even if they are born as humans, they will then be very poor.

before: At that time, the awakening hero knows that living beings are poor. They focus on giving and always give freely. To them, the beautiful four continents are just like a blob of spit. They feel joyful when giving them away, but getting the continents would never bring such joy.
after: The awakening hero knows that living beings are very poor. So the hero focuses on giving and always gives freely. To them, the beautiful four continents are just like a glob of spit. Giving them away brings great joy, but getting the four continents does not.

before: The wise and bright awakening hero thinks of all the living beings in the three realms of existence. They practice generosity, thinking, "May this generosity be given!" They dedicate this to highest awakening for the sake of all beings.
after: The wise and bright awakening hero thinks of all the living beings in the three realms of existence. They think, "May this generosity be given to them!" They practice this generosity. Then they dedicate it to the highest awakening for the sake of all beings.

before: After they practice generosity, they do not hold onto things. They never hope for a result that ripens. Because they are so skilled at giving, they give away everything. When they give just a little, it becomes huge and cannot be measured.
after: After giving generosity, they do not hold on to things. They never hope for a reward or a result that ripens. Because they are so skilled at giving, they give everything away. Even if they give just a little, it grows to become huge and endless.

before: Imagine all the living beings in the three kinds of life. What if every single one of them gave gifts to a Knower of the World? Imagine they gave gifts to the Buddhas, the worthy ones, and the solitary Buddhas. Imagine they did this for endless ages while trying to become a listener.
after: Imagine every single one of the living beings in the three kinds of life. Imagine if all of them gave gifts for endless ages. Imagine they gave these gifts to the Knowers of the World, the Buddhas, the worthy ones, and the solitary Buddhas, while seeking to be a listener.

before: If a wise awakening hero, skilled in clever ways, rejoices in a good deed that stores up goodness and dedicates this stored-up goodness to the highest awakening for the sake of living beings, they outshine all beings by dedicating it.
after: Now imagine a wise awakening hero who is skilled in clever ways. They rejoice in that good deed that stores up goodness. They dedicate this stored-up goodness to the highest awakening to help living beings. By dedicating it, they shine brighter than all those beings!

before: Think of a huge pile of glass jewels. It is completely outshone by a single precious lapis lazuli. It is the same with the huge heap of generosity from all those beings. It is totally outshone by a single awakening hero who chooses to rejoice.
after: Even a huge pile of glass jewels is completely outshone by a single precious lapis lazuli. It is the same for all beings and their vast heap of generosity. They are all outshone by the awakening hero who knows how to rejoice.

before: When an awakening hero gives gifts to beings, they do not say, "This good deed is mine!" They give away the object without holding back. Because of this, their root of goodness will grow with great power. It grows just like a bright, cloudless moon getting fuller in the night sky.
after: Suppose an awakening hero gives gifts to beings. They do not claim the good result as "mine." They give away the object without holding back. Because of this, their root of goodness will grow with great power. It grows like the bright, cloudless moon getting fuller in the sky.

before: This is the sixth topic: teaching the step-by-step path. An awakening hero's generosity stops them from having a life as a hungry ghost. It ends poverty and all mental trouble. While practicing, they gain endless wealth. Through generosity, they help to fully mature living beings who face suffering.
after: This is the sixth topic: teaching the step-by-step path. An awakening hero's generosity stops life as a hungry ghost. It stops poverty and all mental trouble. While practicing this, they gain endless wealth. Through generosity, they help to fully mature living beings who are in suffering.

before: Through good conduct, they avoid a life as an animal. They leave behind the eight unfree states. Then they always find the freedom to practice. Through patience, they gain a great and beautiful body. They become golden and lovely, and others are happy to see them.
after: Through good conduct, they avoid many forms of life as an animal. They leave behind the eight unfree states. This way, they always find the freedom to practice. Through patience, they gain a great and wonderful body. They become golden and beautiful. They are a wonderful sight for others to see.

before: Through steady effort, every quality of goodness stays strong. They find the treasury of the Victorious Ones, which is endless deep knowing. Through deep focus, they leave behind all bad desires. They completely gain knowledge, special knowing, and deep calm.
after: With steady effort, their qualities of goodness will not fade away. They will find the treasury of the Victorious Ones, which is endless deep knowing. With deep focus, they leave behind the bad qualities of worldly desire. They perfectly achieve knowledge, special knowings, and deep calm.

before: Through wisdom, they fully know the nature of things. They completely go beyond all three realms. As the Supreme Leader of People, they turn the precious wheel. They give the teaching to beings to end their suffering.
after: Through wisdom, they fully understand the nature of things. They will completely go beyond all the three realms. Then, as the Supreme Leader of People, they turn the precious wheel. They give the teaching to beings to bring an end to suffering.

before: Chapter seven teaches full awakening in one moment. That awakening hero has made all these things completely perfect.
after: Chapter seven teaches about full awakening in one moment. That awakening hero perfectly finishes all these things.

before: Chapter eight teaches the teaching body. The hero fully holds a perfectly pure land and pure living beings. They fully hold the line of Buddhas and the line of the teaching. They also fully hold the lineage of the community and all things.
after: Chapter eight teaches about the teaching body. The hero fully supports a perfectly pure land and pure living beings. They fully support the line of Buddhas and the line of the teaching. They also fully support the lineage of the community and all things.

before: The Best Healer cures the sickness of wandering beings. He spoke this teaching on wisdom, which includes the path to awakening. Its name is the Collection of Precious Qualities. This path was explained so that all living beings might reach it.
after: The Best Healer cures the sickness of wandering beings. He gave this teaching on wisdom, which holds the path to awakening. This teaching is called the Collection of Precious Qualities, the path to awakening. He explained this path so that all living beings can reach it.
